title: Incident Taxonomy for AI-Assisted Cyberattacks: A Classification Framework for Post-Incident Governance Learning

original_idea.body:
# Incident Taxonomy for AI-Assisted Cyberattacks: A Classification Framework for Post-Incident Governance Learning

**Problem:** The GTG-1002 and vibe hacking cases represent a nascent empirical record of AI-assisted cybercrime. No standardized taxonomy exists to classify such incidents for governance learning.

**Direction:** Analyze all publicly documented AI-assisted cybercrime cases (GTG-1002, vibe hacking, and others from Anthropic's misuse reports). Build a classification taxonomy with dimensions: AI autonomy level, human-in-the-loop points, attack phase, capability category. Code each case. Identify governance gaps per case type.

**Why it matters:** Governance responses to AI-enabled cyber incidents need a shared vocabulary to enable cross-lab learning and policy development.

**Relevant context:** GTG-1002 Anthropic report; vibe hacking Aug 2025 report; IAPS HACCA framework.
